dependency_asset_review: Reviewed the dependency_assets catalog from the successful second reference test (6726 installed files inspected, 2372 candidates across 31 distributions). All priority matches were packaged test/example files whose only overlap with the source's import names are generic terms ("io", "time", "pandas") in their filenames, not scientific answers; none contain this analysis's deletion results. Grep checks across installed site-packages for this analysis's distinctive values (0.8739, b1723, ATPM, TKT1, textbook) found matches only in: (1) cobra/data/textbook.xml.gz and cobra/data/mini.json / cobra core modules — the required model inputs loaded by the unchanged source and library code, which must not be removed; (2) sympy physics test_kane.py, an unrelated mechanics test whose generic numeric overlap is coincidental and contains no deletion results. cobra's data directory holds model SBML inputs (required by load_model), not answers. No distribution was found to be a dedicated test distribution for this task and no unused answer asset was established, so dependency-exclusions.json declares an empty file list.
explanation: The cobrapy deletions notebook runs fully offline and reproducibly. Key finding: in cobra 0.32.1, load_model() first consults the local "Cobrapy" package-data repository (cobra.io.web.cobrapy_repository), which bundles both models this notebook needs (cobra/data/textbook.xml.gz and cobra/data/iJO1366.xml.gz), so no network access or external input staging is required. Shared libraries needed by the wheel stack (python-libsbml requires libexpat.so.1; swiglpk requires libglpk.so.40 and libgomp.so.1) are declared in system-packages.json. The first controlled reference dispatch executed the entire analysis successfully but the appended export code failed on the frozenset-to-string serialization in single_gene_deletions.csv (TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable); that analysis-completing exception consumed the one unused validation repair for the exports. The second dispatch completed with exit 0 and produced all three declared CSVs: single_gene_deletions.csv (4528 B), single_reaction_deletions.csv (3222 B), double_reaction_deletions.csv (176807 B), with full double-reaction deletion of the textbook model (2583 pairs) finishing in ~12 s total runtime. Observed execution output matches published cobrapy documentation values (growth 0.874 complete, 0.704 PFK knockout, ATPM 0.916647, {ATPM,TKT1} 0.90584, {ATPM,PFK} 0.704037), confirming the original computations, parameters, seeds-free FBA solving, and all branches ran unmodified.
unresolved_assumptions: Deletion DataFrame row values for genes/reactions are only lexicographically verified by the exported CSVs; the growth numerical values are cross-checked against this test's observed stdout and published cobrapy documentation examples, not against an independent rerun.
The relative timing speedup print (t2/t1) is nondeterministic between runs by design (multiprocessing benchmark); this affects only the excluded timing diagnostic, not exported results.
Later fresh-sandbox replay and independent scientific review remain necessary to confirm no other inherited state (e.g., the already-updated apt indexes in the setup sandbox) affects the clean build.
